- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon when sentiment is positive or neutral (especially after recent spikes).  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative over the last 5–10 days, especially if the price has recently fallen.  
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings; model should not overshoot downward after a spike unless sentiment confirms sustained bearish momentum.  
- Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence with true trend.  
- For horizon >15 days, reduce forecast sensitivity to sentiment if sentiment is volatile or mixed — use sentiment average over 3–5 days instead of daily.  
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, reduce forecast slope by 15–25% for next 3–5 days to avoid “overcorrection” lag.  
- Do not assume sentiment directly drives price — use sentiment as a modifier, not a primary driver, especially when price action contradicts sentiment.
